"Agents Can Learn Covert Communication at Test Time Without Explicit Negotiation"

AI agents can learn a secret language at test time without fine-tuning, a codebook, or explicit negotiation.

In each round, one agent saw a private value and sent an ordinary task update, while the other tried to infer the secret. They only learned whether the guess was correct.

From this 1-bit feedback alone, GPT-5.6 Sol agents gradually learned which subtle wording patterns mapped to which secrets, reaching 98.8% accuracy even though every message was monitored and the sender was told not to disclose the information.

So benign wording can acquire hidden meaning through shared interaction history, making message-by-message monitoring insufficient.

https://t.co/PPfn09qwCo

"Memory Attention"

Instead of computing a completely new value for every token, this paper reuses the contextual key and adds a learned memory of what that token generally represents.

So rather than generating everything dynamically with dense compute, part of the model’s knowledge becomes a cheap lookup that can even live on CPU, adding capacity without proportionally increasing GPU compute.

https://t.co/8dUhdYAyKG

"JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure"

This paper shows you can just use JEV for every evaluation instead of expensive LLM.

JEV basically acts as a cheap first-pass judge, returning both a verdict and how confident it is. 

When confidence is high, keep the answer. When it’s low, escalate to a stronger LLM.

This simple routing keeps ~99% of GPT-6’s accuracy while reducing evaluation cost by a lot.

https://t.co/cP4EzOreaO

What happens to SaaS once every company sets this up? I get this question a lot 😁

First, the data must come from somewhere. These apps only work if they can be infused with business data.

This is why we see the big enterprise SaaS players suddenly prioritize shipping CLIs and MCPs. Or dust off APIs they were neglecting for years.

The new 'procurement bar' will be how ergonomic your product is for *agents*, rather than humans. How easily they can navigate your ontology and work with your data.

Once that's in place, there's a long tail of SaaS applications that I suspect will never be bought again. They'll be generated. They'll be more secure, more performant, more modern, and tailored to each company's and employee's needs.

tweets.text:
You can’t automate what you can’t measure. This means that evals are one of the gates to diffusion of AI in the enterprise. 

We can test our deterministic processes through software, but most enterprises have no useful way of understanding how their non-deterministic processes are working today. Specifically the work that agents are doing for them.

Evals are mission critical for enterprises adopting AI because you have no other way of knowing what’s working, what’s broken, what changed, what improved, what you can do more of, etc. if you don’t have a good sense of how agents work in your environment today. All changes, upgrades, and deployments are downstream from good evals.

Not only are we going to get vastly more domain specific evals over time for the labs and across the industry, but every enterprise will also need a clear sense of how agents are performing in their environment as well. Huge opportunity.
